subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Universal Design: Parks for All Abilities
description: Learn Universal Design: Parks for All Abilities in one minute.

hook.text: Most playgrounds exclude children in wheelchairs. Universal design means every child can play, climb, and explore.

buildup.text: Inclusive parks use ramps instead of stairs, sensory gardens for blind visitors, and quiet zones for autistic children.

discovery.text: Morgan's Wonderland in San Antonio is the world's first fully accessible theme park. It's free for disabled guests.

twist.text: The ADA requires accessibility but sets only minimum standards. True inclusion goes far beyond legal compliance.

climax.text: Cities like London and Melbourne now audit every park for accessibility and publish the results publicly.

punchline.text: Design for the least able. Everyone benefits.

quiz.question: What is Morgan's Wonderland?
options: A virtual reality park experience for homebound children
The world's first fully accessible theme park with free admission for disabled guests
A chain of indoor playgrounds in shopping malls across Texas
